title: Activation, aging and state of charge dependence of interfacial and kinetic parameters in LaY2Ni9 negative electrode: An electrochemical impedance spectroscopy investigation
content:
Abstract

This study investigates the kinetic and interfacial properties of a LaY2Ni₉ negative electrode using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) during galvanostatic cycling and at various states of charge (SOC). Over 20 cycles, the exchange current density (I0) peaked at 41.82 mA cm−2 at cycle 1 before declining to 20.54 mA cm−2 at cycle 10 due to surface passivation, with a partial rebound to 24.55 mA cm−2 at cycle 20. The double-layer capacitance (Cdl) followed a similar trend, peaking at 283.81 μF cm−2 at cycle 1 reflecting maximum grain fragmentation, and then dropping to 34.54 μF cm−2 at cycle 10. The hydrogen diffusion coefficient (DH) increased steadily from 4.82 × 10–14 to 2034.95 × 10−14 cm2 s−1 across 20 cycles, driven by alloy fragmentation opening new diffusion pathways. SOC analysis (42%–82%) revealed that I₀ peaks at 76% SOC (43.90 mA cm−2), identifying the optimal charge-transfer state, while DH and Cdl increase monotonically and Cev peaks at 80% SOC, indicating saturation near 80%–82%. These results establish LaY2Ni9 as a promising Ni–MH electrode material with superior bulk diffusion kinetics and electrochemical performance governed by both cycling history and hydrogen content.
